dossier.public_summary: A 2.6 Earth-radius flat-bottomed dip repeats every 12.9 days with a duration that matches the star's size, and the signal is in the SPOC and QLP light curves at the same depth while the shallow TESS-SPOC sectors are explained by a calibration offset. No nearby star within a pixel can mimic the dip, and there is no odd-even difference or secondary eclipse. The light-curve variability from starspots and a noisy Gaia solution warrant caution but do not outweigh the planetary evidence.
